catalog_quote: Salvo los dos “motetes” de Cardiel, el acento está anotado en todas las atestaciones vilelas del siglo XVIII, pero no sistemáticamente. En Hervás y Panduro (1786, 1787b), Jolís (1789) y, predominantemente, en Dobrizhoffer (1874) y Hervás y Panduro (1787a) está marcado por un acento grave. En Gilij (1782) está prevalentemente marcado por medio de un acento agudo. Nótese en este sentido que en lengua vilela las palabras aisladas son generalmente oxítonas.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: verbatim on p. 61 of the held Golluscio & Zamponi 2019 PDF, at the stated place. (2) Deciding source: a 2019 open-access phonology/philology article by the leading Vilela specialists; the stress claim is a hedged one-liner about isolation forms, but it is first-hand and is now corroborated by the downloaded Apéndice (12/12 IPA-transcribed 2018-2019 forms from the last speaker are final-stressed) and by the 55/55 final-accented 18th-c. forms tallied earlier. Nothing seen suggests the final-stress coding is wrong. (3) The one work that would clearly improve the record is Golluscio's 2015 De Gruyter grammar sketch (pp. 77-120), which we could not obtain (WAF challenge, closed per Unpaywall/OAPEN); Lozano 1970/2006 and Golluscio & González 2008 are secondary wishes. (4) Status 'adequate': authoritative authors, quote confirmed, independent phonetic corroboration. not 'well

sources.quote: No explicit stress rule (wordlist; no hit for acento/oxítona/sílaba), but contemporary phonetic forms from the last speaker ML (fieldwork 2018-2019) are given with IPA stress marks, e.g. p. A3 '[aˈʔo] ~ [aˈo] ‘sangre’', 'ML reconoce la palabra y la pronuncia [aomanˈman]'; p. A14 '[hoˈtis]'; p. A46 '[toˈke soˈhe]'. All 12 stress-marked forms (script tally) carry stress on the final syllable; 0 non-final.

sources.citation: Machoni de Cerdeña, Antonio (1877). Arte y vocabulario de la lengua lule o tonocoté. Buenos Aires: Coni (= 1732). 259 pp.
sources.note: The work is Machoni's 1732 grammar and vocabulary of LULE / Tonocoté (Glottolog lule1238), reprinted in 1877 with an editor's introduction. Its stress statement (final, with lexical exceptions) is about Lule, not Vilela. Vilela appears only in the 1877 introduction, which quotes Hervás on the Vilela ('Vilelo') and Omoampo dialects and on the Ortega tribes replacing r with d, and prints an eight-item Lule/Vilela wordlist (árbol, cera, frisoles, hijo, olla, oreja, uña, yerba) to argue that Ludewig overstated the Lule-Vilela affinity; nothing there concerns Vilela stress.
